---
title: "`ev_compose()` — multi-contrast patchwork layout"
---

## Purpose

Stack a volcano over its ring for each contrast, then arrange all contrasts into
one `patchwork` figure with a shared legend.

## When to use

The final layout step when you have per-contrast volcano and ring plots and want
a single multi-panel figure for a manuscript or report.

## How it works

Takes two **named** lists — `volcano_plots` and `ring_plots` — that must share
identical names (it aborts otherwise, since names pair the panels). For each
contrast it stacks the volcano above the ring (`patchwork::wrap_plots(ncol = 1)`),
then lays the per-contrast columns out across the page with `nrow` / `ncol` and
collects guides into one shared legend. The result is an `enrichVolcano` object;
its `print` method reports the reconstructible call and a one-line data summary
before rendering. Pass intermediate tibbles via `data` to attach them as the
`ev_data` attribute for that summary.

## Parameters & defaults

| Argument | Default | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `volcano_plots` | — | named list, one ggplot per contrast (required) |
| `ring_plots` | — | named list with **matching names** (required) |
| `nrow` | `NULL` | outer layout rows; let patchwork decide |
| `ncol` | `NULL` | outer layout columns; let patchwork decide |
| `guides` | `"collect"` | one shared legend across panels |
| `data` | `NULL` | optional intermediates attached as `ev_data` for the print summary |

## Literature

No method-specific citation; see [methods](../methods.qmd).

## Example

```r
volcs <- list(CTLvMITO = v1, CTLvDRUG = v2)
rings <- list(CTLvMITO = r1, CTLvDRUG = r2)
ev_compose(volcs, rings, ncol = 2)
```
